amendment.relayed_by: KamaR23-2 (L1) irc 2026-10-21: 'No whole reachable-tree precondition: missing actual required object =>CNE; missing referenced cited blob F23=>CNE; unused historical/unselected blob alone must not refuse.'
amendment.summary: Promisor metadata alone never changes local-object resolution or a clean/failed verdict, including locally unresolved citations and authorized errata matching; no fetch is permitted. Missing objects actually required by audit reads remain could-not-evaluate exit2 with a content-derived reason. A locally unresolved citation known to name unavailable referenced local content is could-not-evaluate rather than proved absence; a bounded missing-object traversal may diagnose that token, but unrelated unavailable objects must not become a blanket precondition. Complete marked versus unmarked twins, including fabricated citations and historical errata-corrected defects, retain identical substantive verdicts. Incomplete but locally sufficient repositories are not refused merely because an unrelated historical blob, branch or unused file is missing.
amendment.original_view_verdict: The initial unknown-citation=>exit2 requirement conflicts with the original supported local-object workflow and is withdrawn prospectively, not counted as achieved.

calibration.question: preregistration expected_after[3] (a missing citation in any promisor-backed repository is unknown => exit 2) versus oracle-amendment-1.json (promisor metadata alone never changes the verdict; a locally unresolved citation is exit 2 only when it is known to name unavailable referenced local content).
calibration.original_reading: expected_after[3] literal: exit 2 for a citation that resolves in no audited repository whenever at least one audited repository is promisor-backed.
calibration.amended_reading: exit 2 only when the unresolved token is known to name unavailable referenced local content; otherwise the ordinary local verdict (exit 1, or exit 0 when an authorized errata row corrects it). The token-scoped rule applies to every store, not only promisor-backed ones.
calibration.note: Both readings are carried side by side. The original view is reported as withdrawn for these rows and is never counted as achieved; the amended view is the graded one.

open_rows.not_graded_because: The traversal scope for diagnosing an unresolved token is contested: closure over all refs would find the token as a hole (exit 2), a selected-root traversal would treat it as proved absent (exit 1). The L1 forbids a broad completeness precondition, so the row is reported, not graded.

supplement.landed: aacbd520 (before the L1 inspected, measured or integrated the candidate)
supplement.chronology: Additional independent CritUnknown hidden-tree fixture, received after the 44-case snapshot and before the L1 candidate source inspection or execution. It is a new adversarial oracle supplement, not a rewritten original expectation.
supplement.authority: build/advice/CritUnknown.md appended qualification; build/out/CritUnknown/hidden_probe.py and hidden-output.txt; local-object contract plus unavailable required evidence policy.
supplement.rule: Only when a citation is unresolved: a known referenced missing matching OID (or prefix) is unavailable; a missing tree/commit may conceal the dependency names and makes that unresolved citation unevaluable. Blob-only unrelated holes do not do so. Never use any missing-object state as an unconditional audit precondition.
supplement.not_unresolved: A known-present blob/tree that merely fails commit peeling is not an absent citation; it keeps the normal wrong-type finding even when unrelated opaque holes exist. A known tag with unavailable target requires an actual dereference and may refuse.
supplement.version_constraint: Do not introduce --missing=print-info or --missing-only, which raise the documented Git floor. A second bounded --filter=blob:none --missing=print walk or equivalent pre-existing Git2.45 primitive can classify non-leaf holes; preserve every existing flag and deadline.
